- Insignia F50 (B) — Pros: Fire TV built-in and Alexa, decent price ($299.99). Cons: Basic HDR10 only, likely similar panel quality to other budget VA sets; choose if you want deep Amazon/Fire integration.

Quick comparison and why D stands out:
- Vizio M-Series (D) — Pros: Dolby Vision/HDR10+, 16 local dimming zones for deeper blacks (great in dim rooms), SmartCast. Cons: 60Hz, VA panel so narrower viewing angles than IPS. Best overall choice for picture quality in a bedroom.
- Pixelight A6 (E) — Pros: Lowest price ($249.99), Dolby Vision, Google TV, DTS Virtual X, 3 HDMI ports, highest sustainability score. Cons: Lesser-known brand (potentially lower long-term reliability) and likely no local dimming; best pick if strictest budget and smart platform preference (Google TV).
- LG UQ7590 (C) — Pros: IPS panel (wide viewing angles), a5 Gen5 processor, webOS and AirPlay 2. Cons: More expensive ($379.99) and IPS means weaker blacks than VA; choose if multiple viewing positions or Apple ecosystem integration matter.
- Samsung TU7000 (A) — Pros: Trusted brand, solid basic performance at $349.99. Cons: Only HDR10, no advanced HDR or local dimming features; less HDR impact than Vizio or Pixelight.
- Insignia F50 (B) — Pros: Fire TV built-in and Alexa, decent price ($299.99). Cons: Basic HDR10 only, likely similar panel quality to other budget VA sets; choose if you want deep Amazon/Fire integration.
